classificationDefinitions.ENFORCED: an executable artefact proves it (test, verifier script, migration, policy or machine-checked contract match) and, where a boundary is declared, a real call site invokes it
classificationDefinitions.DECLARED: a module, document or contract mentions it, but nothing executable proves it
classificationDefinitions.IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED: implementation and tests exist, but the declared boundary patterns match nothing — the capability protects nothing yet

areas.area: Evolution principles, capability discovery and lifecycle transitions are controlled
areas.requirement: Future capabilities require owner/metadata, lifecycle transitions are bounded, proposals route to the correct owner, and change protocol ordering is explicit.

areas.area: Experiments are isolated, expiring, reversible and risk-governed
areas.requirement: Experiments have hypothesis, measurement, owner, expiry and rollback; high-impact experiments receive extra governance; cohorts do not affect unrelated tenants.

areas.area: Rollouts, canaries, feature flags and failure outcomes are controlled
areas.requirement: Rollouts progress through staged environments, canaries are monitored, flags have owners and emergency disablement, and failures preserve reusable engineering knowledge.

areas.area: Deprecation, sunset and migrations preserve rollback and compatibility
areas.requirement: Deprecation and sunset complete all required checks; migrations require dry run, incremental execution, rollback, validation and audit; compatibility is measured.

areas.area: Schema, API, protocol and model changes are backward-compatible or approved
areas.requirement: Schema evolution is additive/backward-compatible, breaking APIs require architecture approval and migration evidence, protocols have fallback controls, and model migration has measurable evidence.

areas.area: Cryptographic, generational and vendor migrations preserve continuity
areas.requirement: Crypto agility, generation migration steps, continuity areas and vendor exit mechanisms are complete before migration claims.

areas.area: Technology, debt, dependency, risk, ADR and evolution memory are recorded
areas.requirement: Technology assessments, debt, dependency health, ADR completeness, evolution risk, known metrics, synthetic-data isolation and engineering memory are explicit.

areas.area: Evolution review, reversibility and autonomy increases are bounded
areas.requirement: Reviews require all dimensions, high-risk changes require reversibility mechanisms, and autonomy increases require evidence and bounded actions.

areas.area: Agent evolution, graduation, ethics, security and supply chain remain governed
areas.requirement: Agent changes preserve permissions/tools/evaluations, graduation requires readiness and score, and ethical, security and supply-chain controls are complete.

areas.area: Evolution incident response, recovery and live execution are wired
areas.requirement: Evolution incidents and recovery execute through durable authorized runtime boundaries with observable rollback and conformance evidence.

limitations: Classification measures the presence of executable evidence, not the correctness or completeness of that evidence.
A DECLARED area is unfinished work, never a false claim — it is reported as such.
An IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED area has a tested implementation that no boundary calls; it is reported, never counted as enforcement.
Evidence patterns are declared per phase in architecture/phase-acceptance/phase-<id>-*.json and must be reviewed when a phase is re-audited.
